task.title: A profile card from the user object
task.html:
Student name

Level: ?

Open profile
task.description: The platform has defined a user object: id, name, avatar, profileUrl, isMentor, email, level. The page has an article#profile card with the attribute data-max-level="10", and inside it img#avatar, h2#profile-name, p#level-text, the link a#profile-link, the checkbox #mentor and the field #email. Write a function fillProfile(person) that fills the card with data from person: 1) the name - into #profile-name with .text(); 2) give #avatar src = person.avatar and alt = "Photo: " + name in one .attr() call with an object; 3) give #profile-link the attribute href = person.profileUrl; 4) tick or untick the #mentor checkbox with .prop("checked", person.isMentor); 5) write person.email into the #email field with .val(); 6) save person.id in the card's data: .data("userId", ...); 7) read the maximum level from data-max-level with .data("maxLevel") and write the text "Level 3 of 10" into #level-text, where 3 is person.level; 8) call fillProfile(user). The function must work when called again with a different student. Do not use document.querySelector, innerHTML or .html().

tests.name: A name like "<b>..." is output as text, not as markup
tests.fail: Output the name only with .text(): then the tags are shown as letters and do not run.

tests.name: The avatar has the correct src and alt
src and alt are set in one .attr call with an object
tests.fail: Pass an object to .attr(): .attr({ src: ..., alt: ... }).

tests.name: The link leads to the profile
The checkbox updates even after it has been clicked
tests.check: (() => { const cb = document.querySelector("#mentor"); cb.click(); fillProfile(user); return cb.checked === true; })()
tests.fail: After a click, the attribute no longer controls the checkbox. Change the property: .prop("checked", ...), not .attr().

tests.name: Calling again with isMentor: false unticks the checkbox
tests.check: (() => { fillProfile({ ...user, isMentor: false }); return document.querySelector("#mentor").checked === false; })()
tests.fail: Pass person.isMentor to .prop("checked", ...) - true or false.

tests.name: The email field contains the student's address
The student's id is saved in .data("userId")
tests.fail: $("#profile").data("userId", person.id); - the value stays a number.

tests.name: The maximum level is read from data-max-level
tests.fail: Do not type 10 by hand: take the number from $("#profile").data("maxLevel").

tests.name: Calling again with a different student rewrites the card
tests.check: (() => { const email = document.querySelector("#email"); email.value = "typed@mail.ru"; email.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true })); fillProfile({ id: 5, name: "Boris", avatar: "img/boris.png", profileUrl: "https://jlearn.space/u/boris", isMentor: false, email: "boris@example.com", level: 7 }); return document.querySelector("#profile-name").textContent === "Boris" && document.querySelector("#avatar").getAttribute("alt") === "Photo: Boris" && document.querySelector("#profile-link").getAttribute("href") === "https://jlearn.space/u/boris" && email.value === "boris@example.com" && $("#profile").data("userId") === 5 && document.querySelector("#level-text").textContent === "Level 7 of 10"; })()
tests.fail: Inside the function, use the person parameter, not user. Fill the field with .val(): .attr("value") does not change what the user has already typed.

tests.name: The program runs without errors
tests.fail: Check that the fillProfile function is declared and called, and that the selectors have no typos.

hints: Name: $("#profile-name").text(person.name); - tags in the name will show up as letters.
An object in .attr(): $("#avatar").attr({ src: person.avatar, alt: `Photo: ${person.name}` });
For a checkbox, use the property, not the attribute: $("#mentor").prop("checked", person.isMentor);
An input field is filled with .val(person.email).
data-max-level is read as .data("maxLevel") and becomes a number right away.
Inside the function, write person everywhere, not user: then the function works for any student.

questions.question: A user entered the name . Which call safely outputs it to the page?
questions.explanation: .text() inserts the string as text: the tags are shown as letters and do not run. .html() would parse the string as markup - that is XSS.

questions.question: What does $("#email").val() return if the user typed anna@mail.ru into the field and the markup has value=""?
options: "anna@mail.ru" - the current value of the field
questions.explanation: .val() reads the value property - what is in the field right now. The value attribute only stores the initial value.

questions.question: A checkbox <input type="checkbox" id="agree">. The user ticked it. What does $("#agree").prop("checked") return?
questions.explanation: .prop() reads a property of the DOM element - the current state, true or false. .attr("checked") would return undefined: there is no attribute in the markup.

questions.question: Match the task with the jQuery method.
pairs: The current value of an input field
The link address from the markup
questions.explanation: Field value - .val(), attribute - .attr(), live state - .prop(), data-* data - .data().

questions.question: Which calls make the #send button inactive?
questions.explanation: A button is disabled by the presence of the attribute or by a truthy property. The string "false" is not empty, so it is truthy too - a tricky mistake. removeAttr removes the disabled state.

questions.question: <div id="c" data-lessons="10">. What does console.log($("#c").data("lessons") + 1) print?
questions.explanation: .data() turns "10" into the number 10, so 10 + 1 = 11. With .attr("data-lessons") you would get a string and the concatenation "101".

questions.question: You ran $("#c").data("status", "done"). What will you see on the #c element in DevTools?
options: No data-status attribute: .data() keeps the value in jQuery's memory
questions.explanation: The .data() setter does not change the HTML. If you need the attribute in the markup (for example, for CSS), use .attr("data-status", "done").

questions.question: Complete the call that removes the title attribute from #photo: $("#photo").______("title"). Enter only the method name.
questions.explanation: .removeAttr("title") removes the attribute completely instead of making it empty.

questions.question: Which lines give an image both src and alt?
questions.explanation: Several attributes are set with an object or with a chain of setters. .attr() ignores extra arguments.

questions.question:
The page has three

: "a", "b", "c". What will the second paragraph contain after $(".note").text((index, old) => `${index + 1}) ${old}`)?
options: An error: you cannot pass a function to .text()
questions.explanation: The function is called for each element: index is the number from zero, old is the current text. For the second paragraph index = 1, old = "b".

questions.question: Match plain JavaScript with jQuery.
questions.explanation: jQuery does the same thing, but for all found elements at once.

questions.question: <div id="u" data-user-id="5">. Which key name should you pass to .data() if you write in camelCase, as this course does? Enter the name without quotes.
questions.explanation: Hyphens turn into camelCase: data-user-id → .data("userId"), like dataset.userId in plain JavaScript.
